Synopsis:
    An Egyptian deportee held in Equatorial Guinea under a US third-country deportation arrangement has been taken into incommunicado custody after speaking to Reuters about alleged police violence against migrants. Security forces seized detainees' phones, citing the Reuters report. The case escalates scrutiny of Trump administration deals with African governments to offload deportees — many of whom had prior US court protection from persecution. Human rights groups are demanding accountability and have already filed a complaint at the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights.
